lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- The Gallery
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 7 -- The Gallery

listenings.text: Last spring, I finally saw the Sistine Chapel in Rome. I waited two hours in line, and inside it was very crowded. You are not allowed to take photos, and the guards keep saying: silence, please. But then you look up. The ceiling was painted by Michelangelo more than five hundred years ago, and he did most of it alone. It was cleaned and restored a few decades ago, so the colors are bright again. Today the chapel is visited by thousands of people every day, and I understand why. Some places are famous for a reason. I stood there for forty minutes, and my neck hurt for two days.

People always tell me: you have to see the big museums. Honestly, I do not like them very much. They are too crowded, and you see the paintings through other people's phones. My favorite place in Portugal is a small church in a village near the sea. Nobody knows who built it. The walls are covered with blue and white tiles, and every tile was painted by hand about three hundred years ago. There is no line and no guided tour. An old man opens the door in the morning and closes it at night. I sat there alone for an hour. For me, that was the real masterpiece.
